title: What Is Attention?
hook: Attention lets a model decide what to focus on: it scores how relevant each piece of input is to the current question, then blends them by those scores.
key_points: Attention is a learned, content-based lookup — no fixed wiring, the weights depend on the inputs.
Each query is compared against a set of keys to produce relevance weights.
The output is a weighted sum of values, dominated by the best-matching keys.
Self-attention applies this within one sequence, relating every position to every other.
content_html: Attention is a mechanism that lets a neural network look over all its inputs and decide which ones matter for the task at hand. Lilian Weng's widely read overview frames it as a content-based weighted lookup: a query is matched against keys to get relevance scores, and the result is a weighted average of the corresponding values. Self-attention is the special case where a sequence attends to itself, letting every word relate to every other word.
extra_html:
How it works

You start with three views of the data: queries, keys, and values. For a given query, you measure how well it matches each key — typically with a dot product — and turn those match scores into weights that sum to one. The output is the sum of all values weighted by those scores, so values whose keys matched the query best contribute the most. Because the weights are computed from the data itself, the model effectively learns what to pay attention to rather than relying on fixed connections.

Why it matters

Attention solved a long-standing problem: older sequence models squeezed everything into one fixed-size summary and tended to forget distant context. By letting any position directly reference any other, attention captures long-range relationships and does it in parallel rather than step by step. This idea is the foundation of Transformers and nearly every modern large language model, so understanding it unlocks how today's AI actually reads and reasons over text.

related.title: Attention Is All You Need
related.hook: Drop recurrence and convolution, keep only attention — and you get a model that trains in parallel and powers nearly every LLM since.

related.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
related.hook: Cramming a whole sentence into one vector loses information. This 2014 paper let the decoder look back at relevant source words at each step — the original attention mechanism.

related.hook: Before you tackle the Transformer paper, watch a sentence flow through one — query, key, value, and all — in clear pictures.

prereqs.title: How Neural Networks Learn: Backpropagation
prereqs.hook: A neural net learns by asking, for every weight, 'how much did you contribute to my mistake?' Backprop answers all of them at once.
